title: Zebra Stripes, Sinking Slabs, and the Heat-Pipe Earth: Plate Tectonics, Whole-Mantle Convection & the Great Subduction-Onset Debate — How Wegener's ridiculed continental drift became geophysics' supreme unifying law; Vine & Matthews's symmetric seafloor geomagnetic tape recorder & Jason Morgan's rigid spherical Euler-pole kinematics; why Forsyth & Uyeda proved sinking slabs pull plates 10x harder than ridges push while asthenosphere drags backward; global seismic tomography tracking Farallon & Tethys slabs past 660 km to the core-mantle boundary; GPS/SLR/GRACE bounding Earth expansion to 0.1 mm/yr vs. the fierce Archean heat-pipe stagnant-lid to Neoproterozoic subduction-onset war

teenKit.tldr: For decades, scientists laughed at the idea that continents could drift, but modern geophysics proved that giant slabs of Earth's crust are constantly sinking, colliding, and tearing apart at the speed your fingernails grow.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how tectonic plates move helps us predict catastrophic earthquakes and volcanic eruptions before they strike, protecting millions of lives worldwide.
keyTakeaways: Alfred Wegener's ridiculed continental drift theory was ultimately vindicated when researchers discovered symmetric magnetic stripes frozen into the ocean floor acting like a planetary tape recorder.
Cold, sinking oceanic slabs (called 'slab pull') do the heavy lifting in plate tectonics, pulling plates down ten times harder than ocean ridges push them.
Using global GPS and seismic tomography, scientists can track tectonic plates plunging thousands of kilometers deep all the way to Earth's core-mantle boundary.

vocab.meaning: A region where one heavy tectonic plate slides underneath another and plunges deep into Earth's mantle.
The mathematical geometry used to describe how rigid blocks spin and move across the curved surface of a sphere like Earth.
A technique that uses earthquake shockwaves like a medical CT scan to map out the hidden, deep interior of our planet.
A radical theory suggesting early Earth cooled itself through massive volcanic heat pipes instead of modern plate tectonics.

quiz.question: What primary force actually drives the motion of tectonic plates?
options: Ocean currents pushing against the shores
Cold sinking slabs pulling the plates downward
The rotation of the moon spinning the crust
Expanding Earth swelling from the inside out
quiz.explanation: Forsyth and Uyeda proved that the heavy pull of cold, sinking oceanic slabs drives plate movement far more powerfully than ridges push.

quiz.question: What did Vine and Matthews discover on the ocean floor that helped prove plate tectonics?
options: Symmetric zebra-striped magnetic reversals frozen in the rock
Ancient human artifacts preserved in deep trenches
Pure gold deposits lining mid-ocean boundaries
Massive underground tunnels carved by ancient magma flows
quiz.explanation: Magnetic minerals in cooling basalt lock in Earth's magnetic field direction, creating a mirror-image stripe pattern on either side of ocean ridges.

quiz.question: How fast do tectonic plates typically move across Earth's surface?
options: At the speed of a racing car
About as fast as human hair or fingernails grow
Roughly the speed of a walking pedestrian
They never actually move at all today
quiz.explanation: Plates creep along at roughly 20 millimeters per year, which matches the leisurely pace of your growing fingernails.
